question: Which Plate defaults and public plugin contracts serve a product job, and which duplicate an adequate Plite owner?
method: best-api-review/history-v2; first-principles and maximum-value hard-cut comparison
trigger: User selected ledger item 6, plate-core, and invoked Best API Review.
requirements: Infer installation, schema, dependencies, services, reads and updates without caller annotations or casts.
Preserve configured-family access, rejection of unrelated same-name descriptors, serialized schema identity and application overrides.
Preserve per-editor configuration and stores, atomic candidate cleanup and active-transaction ownership.
Keep raw Plite independent of Plate product policy; keep headless/static, live React, optional-feature and detached tooling jobs truthful.
Keep independent Plate feature reviews separate, including math and emoji. Assessment does not authorize implementation or publication.
evidenceReuse: No direct earlier review exists for this question. Rechecked current owners and real consumers. The 2026-09-11 Plite-core review retains canonical atomic extension composition; the 2026-08-30 facade and 2026-08-28 package plans supply historical constraints, not current proof. Their package/headless directions are reaffirmed; their incidental public or private machinery is not treated as a hard law.
summary: Pursue contract design for one installed capability identity and lookup; retain Plate product semantics and leave replacement runtime unaccepted pending scale proof.
alternatives: Keep/configure: existing correctness contracts pass, but caller configuration cannot remove the second identity mapping and duplicate installed lookup.
Change existing API: pursue one canonical installed reference and inferred Plate product projection; settle exact-descriptor versus configured-family semantics before implementation.
Add primitive: only a neutral missing descriptor/publication capability can earn addition; reject another adapter registry, public compiler graph or store.

Delete/merge/inline: strongest direction removes the separate installed Plate identity/lookup protocol and selector remapping where the canonical owner can perform it; product-only lowering remains private.
Move ownership: Plite owns installed identity, dependency admission and schema-handle resolution. Plate keeps rules, configuration, product stores, codecs and React publication.

Replace architecture: reject merging all Plate policy into raw Plite or copying framework behavior into kits. A particular unified runtime remains provisional; no speed claim or accepted runtime architecture is inferred from source.
Base/React conversion: empty adapters alone do not justify eliminating React authoring; real paragraph shortcuts and mounted-view slot contexts require inference and dependency-boundary parity.
proofLimits: Observed 38 Base/plugin-access/codec-context tests, 18 React constructor/adapter tests and 20 package-proof runner fixture tests passed. No current packed-release, full typecheck, browser, native-device, performance or external-consumer proof. No replacement runtime is accepted. A paired current/target scale comparison remains required before adoption. Shared-checkout source may change after this recorded snapshot.
